'''''Iris lutescens''''', the '''Crimean iris'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fws.gov/species/crimean-iris-iris-lutescens|title=''Iris lutescens'' {{!}} Crimean Iris|publisher=[[USFWS]]}}</ref> or '''dwarf iris''', is a [[rhizome|rhizomatous]] flowering plant in the [[genus]] ''[[Iris (plant)|Iris]]''. It is [[native plant|native]] to North East [[Spain]], Southern [[France]] and [[Italy]]. It is found on rocky or sandy hillsides or in woodlands.<ref name=perennial/>
[[File:Iris lutescens (flowers).jpg|thumb|left]]
It grows up to {{cvt|30|cm|in}} tall, with broad leaves (about {{cvt|2.5|cm}} wide),<ref name=perennial/> producing yellow or violet flowers in spring (March–April). It prefers full sun, a slightly acid soil, and dry conditions during its dormant period in the summer. It is very hardy, down to {{cvt|-20|C|F}} or less.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

This plant is cultivated as an ornamental plant in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions. In the UK it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=''Iris lutescens''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/9306/Iris-lutescens/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=25 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 53 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 13 March 2018}}</ref>
